_purpose: Shared catalog of baits/lures for the Fish Detail page. Species link to these by id in species_bait_map_v1.json. Count per species is whatever the research supports, never padded.
_regulation_note_policy: Every item has a wi_regulation_note. Where Wisconsin bait rules (live baitfish, invasive-species, NR 19/20) have not yet been researched for the item, the value is the literal string 'NOT_YET_RESEARCHED' plus a reason, and the UI must not present the item as cleared for use on all waters.

minnows_live.name: Live minnows
minnows_live.description: Live baitfish; the main forage of walleye.
minnows_live.wi_regulation_note: Wild-caught minnows may be used only on the water they were collected from and may not be moved away live. Minnows bought from a Wisconsin bait dealer can be reused on the same water, or elsewhere if no lake or river water was added to the container (up to 2 gallons of water, no other fish in it). Minnow harvest is closed on VHS known and suspect waters. A minnow 8 inches or longer may only be fished with a quick-strike rig or a non-offset circle hook (NR 20.06(11)).

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin DNR. How VHS rules affect anglers (Q&A).
wi_regulation_sources.quote: On non-VHS waters, you can collect minnows for personal use as long as you only use them for bait on the water you collected them from, but it is illegal to transport any such live minnows away from the water body where you caught them.

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin DNR. How VHS rules affect anglers (Q&A).
wi_regulation_sources.quote: Anglers can take minnows bought from a Wisconsin bait dealer (which includes Wisconsin registered fish farms) away from a lake or river and use them again on that same waterbody. Anglers can also take minnows bought from a Wisconsin bait dealer (which includes Wisconsin registered fish farms) away from a waterbody and use them elsewhere if no lake or river water was added to the bait container. In both of these instances, you can move the amount of water needed to keep the minnows alive, up to 2 gallons. No other fish may be held in the minnow container.

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin DNR. How VHS rules affect anglers (Q&A).
wi_regulation_sources.quote: No person may harvest minnows from these waters, except that suckers may be harvested but may not be transported away live.

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin Administrative Code, Chapter NR 20, s. NR 20.06 (as published on the Wisconsin Legislature website).
wi_regulation_sources.quote: Fish with a minnow 8 inches or longer unless using a quick-strike rig that the person attempts to hook immediately into the mouth of a fish upon indication of a bite or unless using a non-offset circle hook.

leeches.name: Leeches
leeches.wi_regulation_note: Worms, leeches, insects and larvae are generally legal bait, but all water must be drained from fishing equipment and containers when you leave the water (except up to 2 gallons holding minnows), including containers holding leeches or aquatic insects.

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin DNR. How VHS rules affect anglers (Q&A).
wi_regulation_sources.quote: No, other types of live baits such as worms, leeches, insects, larvae, are generally still legal to use. However, under the rules, all water is required to be drained from all equipment and containers used for fishing when you leave the water (except for the up to 2 gallons holding minnows).

small_bullheads.name: Small bullheads
small_bullheads.wi_regulation_note: Fish other than minnows may be used as bait, but only fish caught in that water may be used on that water unless dead and preserved without refrigeration or freezing; live game or rough fish generally cannot be moved away from the water; fish used as bait count toward your daily bag limit; suckers may not be transported away live. NR 20.06(11) limits fishing with a 'minnow' 8 inches or longer to quick-strike rigs or non-offset circle hooks - the pages read do not say whether it applies to suckers, so check the current regulations for large live bait.

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin DNR. Using fish as bait.
wi_regulation_sources.quote: Fish other than minnows may be used as bait.

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin DNR. Using fish as bait.
wi_regulation_sources.quote: Only fish caught in that water can be used as bait on that water, unless they are dead and have been preserved by a method that does not require refrigeration or freezing. Live games or rough fish cannot be moved away from water, with a few very limited exceptions. Also, keep in mind that any fish that are caught and used as bait must be counted towards your daily bag limit.

spawn.name: Spawn (fish eggs)
spawn.wi_regulation_note: Fish eggs (spawn) from Lake Michigan and its tributaries may be used on Lake Superior only if first preserved without refrigeration or freezing (WDNR suggests not using Lake Michigan spawn on Lake Superior at all); only Lake Superior spawn may be used fresh there. Lake Michigan and Lake Superior system spawn may be used on Lake Michigan and its tributaries without preserving. Commercial artificial and preserved spawn are options.

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin DNR. How VHS rules affect anglers (Q&A).
wi_regulation_sources.quote: Fish eggs, or spawn from Lake Michigan and its tributaries, can only be used on Lake Superior if it is first preserved by a method that does not require refrigeration or freezing. ... ONLY spawn collected from Lake Superior and its tributaries may be used to fish Lake Superior and its tributaries without being preserved. ... Lake Michigan and Lake Superior system spawn may be used on Lake Michigan and its tributaries without being preserved. Anglers have reported good success using commercially produced artificial and preserved spawn on Great Lakes waters.

alewives.name: Alewives (fish bait)
alewives.wi_regulation_note: Dead fish may be used as bait only if caught on the water being fished or preserved without refrigeration or freezing (commercially produced dead bait that needs no refrigeration is allowed); dead bait of any type may be used on Lake Michigan and Green Bay. Frozen fish may not be used on other waters unless thawed and preserved, except on Lake Michigan and its tributaries.

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin DNR. How VHS rules affect anglers (Q&A).
wi_regulation_sources.quote: Only if they were caught on the water you are fishing or have been preserved in a manner that does not require refrigeration or freezing. ... You can also use commercially produced dead baits as long as they do not require refrigeration. Dead bait of any type can be used on Lake Michigan and waters of Green Bay or on the water where the bait was harvested.

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin DNR. How VHS rules affect anglers (Q&A).
wi_regulation_sources.quote: Frozen fish CANNOT be used on any water other than where they were caught (EXCEPTION: frozen bait can be used on Lake Michigan and its tributaries upstream to the first barrier impassable to fish) unless they are first thawed and then preserved in a method that does not require refrigeration or freezing for long term storage.

minnows_crappie.name: Small 'crappie minnows'
minnows_crappie.description: Small live minnows sold as crappie minnows.
minnows_crappie.wi_regulation_note: Wild-caught minnows may be used only on the water they were collected from and may not be moved away live. Minnows bought from a Wisconsin bait dealer can be reused on the same water, or elsewhere if no lake or river water was added to the container (up to 2 gallons of water, no other fish in it). Minnow harvest is closed on VHS known and suspect waters. A minnow 8 inches or longer may only be fished with a quick-strike rig or a non-offset circle hook (NR 20.06(11)).

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin DNR. How VHS rules affect anglers (Q&A).
wi_regulation_sources.quote: On non-VHS waters, you can collect minnows for personal use as long as you only use them for bait on the water you collected them from, but it is illegal to transport any such live minnows away from the water body where you caught them.

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin DNR. How VHS rules affect anglers (Q&A).
wi_regulation_sources.quote: Anglers can take minnows bought from a Wisconsin bait dealer (which includes Wisconsin registered fish farms) away from a lake or river and use them again on that same waterbody. Anglers can also take minnows bought from a Wisconsin bait dealer (which includes Wisconsin registered fish farms) away from a waterbody and use them elsewhere if no lake or river water was added to the bait container. In both of these instances, you can move the amount of water needed to keep the minnows alive, up to 2 gallons. No other fish may be held in the minnow container.

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin DNR. How VHS rules affect anglers (Q&A).
wi_regulation_sources.quote: No person may harvest minnows from these waters, except that suckers may be harvested but may not be transported away live.

wi_regulation_sources.citation: Wisconsin Administrative Code, Chapter NR 20, s. NR 20.06 (as published on the Wisconsin Legislature website).
wi_regulation_sources.quote: Fish with a minnow 8 inches or longer unless using a quick-strike rig that the person attempts to hook immediately into the mouth of a fish upon indication of a bite or unless using a non-offset circle hook.
